stance_basis: position paper explicitly challenges the environmental wisdom of allowing ORVs on federal lands and calls for phasing out motors from public lands
summary: The Milwaukee Audubon Society, through its president David Tillotson, submitted a formal position paper strongly opposing the Draft Environmental Impact Statement on ORV use on public lands. The Society argues that the draft statement improperly institutionalizes ORV use on federal lands without first questioning whether such use should be permitted at all, and documents numerous instances of ecological harm caused by ORVs. They call for a phasing out of motorized vehicles from public lands, limiting ORV use to private lands and manufacturer-provided areas, with exceptions only for emergency, law enforcement, and patrol purposes.
complaint_summary: President David Tillotson transmits the Milwaukee Audubon Society's position paper on ORV use on public lands to the Department of Interior, requesting it be forwarded to the proper agency in time for the hearing.

statement.text:
14 Mar 1973
Mr. Nathaniel Reed US Department of Interior Washington, D.C. 20340
Dear Mr. Reed,
Attached is a position paper of the Milwaukee Audubon Society dealing with the subject of Off The Road Recreational Vehicles on Public Land.
It is our understanding that public reaction was invited to a draft statement on ORV use issued by one of Interior's subagencies - the Eureau of Outdoor Recreation.
We trust that you will see that our position on the ORV matter gets to the proper agency in time for the hearing on this matter.
Sincerely
David Tillotson
President - Milwaukee
Audubon Society
12259 Underwood Fkwy
Wauwatosa, Wis 53226
CC: Cynthia Wilson (Natl Audubon)
CC: Ed Brigham (Natl Midwest Audubon Rep)
